source.name: FTC, Safeguards Rule: What Your Business Needs to Know

exemption.text: Section 314.4(b)(1), (d)(2), (h) and (i) do not apply to financial institutions that maintain customer information concerning fewer than five thousand consumers.

questions.question: Is one named person designated to implement and supervise the information security program?
questions.fix: Name one person (an employee, or someone at a service provider with a senior person at the firm overseeing them) and record it in the written plan.

questions.question: Is there a written risk assessment with criteria for evaluating risks to customer information?
questions.fix: Write down where customer information lives, what could go wrong, and how each risk is rated and handled.

questions.question: Is the risk assessment repeated periodically and after changes?
questions.fix: Set a review date, at least yearly, and after any change of systems or providers.

questions.question: Is access to customer information limited to people who need it, and reviewed periodically?
questions.fix: Give each person their own login, remove access when roles change, and review the access list on a schedule.

questions.question: Is there an inventory of the data held and the systems, devices and people that handle it?
questions.fix: List every system, device and storage location that holds customer information.

questions.question: Is customer information encrypted both when stored and when sent?
questions.fix: Turn on full-disk encryption, use an encrypted portal or encrypted email for client documents, or have the Qualified Individual approve an alternative control in writing.

questions.question: Is the security of the software used to handle customer information evaluated, whether built in-house or bought?
questions.fix: Review each vendor's security documentation before use and record the review.

questions.question: Is multi-factor authentication required for anyone accessing a system that holds customer information?
questions.fix: Turn on multi-factor authentication for every system that holds customer information, or have the Qualified Individual approve an equivalent control in writing.

questions.question: Is customer information securely disposed of no later than two years after it was last used, unless there is a business or legal reason to keep it?
questions.fix: Adopt a retention schedule, document the reasons for keeping older records, and dispose of the rest securely.

questions.question: Are changes to systems and networks evaluated for security impact before they are made?
questions.fix: Before adding or changing a system, device or provider, record a short security review.

questions.question: Is user activity logged and monitored to detect unauthorized access?
questions.fix: Keep logging enabled on systems that hold customer information and review the logs on a schedule.

questions.question: Are the safeguards regularly tested or monitored to confirm they work?
questions.fix: Schedule regular checks: restore a backup, confirm patches, test that former staff cannot log in.

questions.question: Is there continuous monitoring, or annual penetration testing plus vulnerability assessments every six months?
questions.fix: Arrange continuous monitoring, or an annual penetration test and six-monthly vulnerability scans, usually through an IT provider.

questions.question: Do all staff receive security awareness training, with refreshers?
questions.fix: Train everyone at hiring and at least yearly, and keep signed records.

questions.question: Are service providers chosen for their ability to protect customer information, bound by contract to do so, and reassessed periodically?
questions.fix: List every provider with access to customer information, check each contract for security terms, and review them on a schedule.

questions.question: Is the security program updated when operations, staff or threats change, and after testing?
questions.fix: Review the written plan at least yearly and after any incident or material change.

questions.question: Is there a written incident response plan covering roles, communications, remediation, documentation and a post-incident review?
questions.fix: Write a short plan: who decides, who is called, how systems are contained, who is notified, and how lessons are recorded.

questions.question: Does the Qualified Individual report in writing at least yearly to the board or a senior officer?
questions.fix: Have the Qualified Individual give the owner or board a written yearly report on the program and any incidents.

questions.question: Does the firm know it must notify the FTC within 30 days of discovering unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted information of 500 or more consumers?
questions.fix: Add the FTC notification step and the 30-day deadline to the incident procedure.
